diagnosis: After candidate generation, eight previously correct SearchQA short answers became longer responses and lost exact-match success; the localization report also disagreed with authoritative domain counts.
mechanism: Strengthened completion and verification instructions in both Action and Planning prompts; providers and model weights were unchanged.
unknowns: Both prompts changed together; individual instruction effects have not been isolated.
The historical grader had separate Code and tool-adapter issues; old scores serve as diagnostic evidence only.

when: Proposed changes affect Action/Planning completion requirements or answer detail
recommend: Identify the submission interface and successful parent behavior before designing a candidate. After evaluation, inspect new successes and regressions by task ID, especially short answers becoming long responses.
avoid_when: Do not generalize one failed prompt candidate to all HARNESS changes.
expected_signal: Previously correct short answers remain correct after presentation changes.
unknowns: This preventive procedure has not yet been validated with a new controlled candidate.

diagnosis: Some failed trajectories stored plans or speculation in Memory and answered without supporting observations.
mechanism: Changed the Memory provider and Action/Planning prompts together to distinguish unverified notes from tool observations and require evidence for factual answers.
unknowns: A combined intervention cannot isolate each change.
Unchanged domain totals do not imply no per-task regressions.
Later scores on different batches do not establish paired generalization.

when: SearchQA Memory states plans or speculation as confirmed facts
recommend: Inspect factual status in Memory and observation use in Action/Planning; generate a complete candidate through the three RSIFlow stages.
avoid_when: No observed evidence implicates Memory in the error
unknowns: No controlled evidence of improved Code performance

diagnosis: Successful parent trajectories concentrate in SearchQA and a small number of tool tasks; no Code successes were recorded.
mechanism: Ran one LoRA SFT epoch on the accepted B2 harness. Historical training reported 211 positive samples; only the model checkpoint changed.
unknowns: Use the actual SFT filtering receipt for sample counts; task-success counts are not training-example counts.
Gains on the same batch do not establish generalization to independent tasks.
No positive samples in a domain means no direct supervision, not that transfer is impossible.
Historical Code scoring errors were fixed; zero historical Code scores do not establish permanent model incapacity.

when: Verified parent successes are eligible for training
recommend: Assess MODEL feasibility using current failures, positive-example domain coverage, and actual SFT filtering receipts; predict the affected domains before training.
avoid_when: Switching to MODEL merely because HARNESS was tried repeatedly
Mistaking tool or grading failures for model-capability failures
Assuming SFT must improve a target domain without direct supervision
expected_signal: More net new successes while preserving successful behavior
unknowns: No real ARTIFACTS intervention is available; its relative quality is unknown.
Acceptance uses paired scores on the same batch; independent validation is for reporting only.

signature: model_call_count=0 and Tool.inputs rejects JSON Schema unions such as ['string','null']
routing_effect: This exception does not establish a capability defect in any Task component; affected tasks remain in the full paired denominator.
recommend: Inspect the actual exception to determine its source and rerun both parent and candidate with the same repaired executor.
unknowns: Zero model calls alone do not identify this failure; confirm the exception signature.

signature: Call-based expectations wrap [True]/[False], while the function returns True/False, causing grading errors.
routing_effect: Old failure labels cannot permanently determine Code capability or SFT eligibility; remeasure with the same repaired grader.
recommend: Check the official call-based wrapper convention and post-fix evaluation records.
unknowns: Not all Code failures arise from wrapping.
